scope: Seven fitted rigid portrait heads; bodies, rigs and animation samples retain their accepted geometry and data.

method.baseline: Embedded pre-proportion original GLB recovered with recoverHeadProportionBase
method.space: World rest coordinates, unchanged indexed triangles
method.old_new_normal_opposition: Dot product of old and fitted geometric face normals below zero. This is a direction comparison, not proof of a negative deformation Jacobian.
method.smooth_normal_mismatch: Originally geometric-to-mean-vertex-normal alignment above 0.2, fitted alignment below -0.1.
method.timing: Positions and normals audited before final tangent-only correction. Final tangent changes do not change these triangle results.

interpretation: The transition is orientation-preserving at evaluated vertices; the main face above the collar transition scales uniformly.

The strict triangle-direction audit is not zero. Most affected Nika triangles are lower rear hair near world Y 1.35–1.40 and Z +0.12–+0.19; the opposed-direction source area is approximately 0.00705 square metres, 0.148 percent of the head surface.
A positive smooth Jacobian alone does not guarantee that coarse triangle chords retain the direction of their original face normal. This audit does not claim zero folded or flipped-looking faces.
The parent inspected the current rear hair/collar closeup and accepted the prototype without significant new visible holes.
The final seven-asset automated checks separately verify the locked collar, preserved body/rig/UV/textures/clips, finite unit normals, orthogonal unit tangents and transformed blink deltas.
limits: No new GPU generation or body refit was performed.
Rest geometry audit does not replace visual inspection at every camera angle.
Hair crown bounds include buns, bobs and other hairstyle volume; they are not anatomical skull landmarks.
